metadata.color_semantics: Fidelity claude palette. ONE terracotta #D97757 event per beat, always marking THE THING THAT WAS BROKEN OR IS STILL OPEN — the audit failure, the unposted draft. The accent tracks honesty, not decoration.
metadata.note: GENRE: first-person progress report, not a concept explainer. HONESTY (hard): every claim comes from the human's own account of her week. NO tool counts, NO dates, NO metrics, NO description of what the Ogilvy tool does (not supplied — the reel says only that the article is written and unposted). NO claim the article is published. beats.narration_text: The Humanitarians AI tools page had been broken for a long time. Nobody could really use any of it. So before I could write about a single tool, I had to fix the thing underneath. Here's the week.

show.event: Cream page, spark, serif greeting 'Sawubona, Yatra' above the composer
The ask types itself in
Terracotta send button arms — the ONE accent event
Running indicator: 'ordering the week…'
Three result lines stagger in — the ask lands ANSWERED (COLD OPEN LAW)

props.command: I market the Humanitarians AI tools: I make graphics, post them on LinkedIn, and write a Substack piece on how I actually used each tool myself. Problem — the tools page has been broken for a long time. Where do I start: the writing, or the thing underneath it?
output: start underneath — a broken page makes every post a promise you can't keep
audit every tool first, then schedule the writing
one tool a week beats one big launch

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Yatra, and I work on the Humanitarians AI tools. I market them — graphics, LinkedIn posts, and a Substack article on how I actually used each tool myself. This video is about the week I stopped writing and fixed the foundation instead. Stay with me and you'll see what a week of unglamorous maintenance actually buys you.

show.event: Four steps draw in around a loop, one at a time as each is named: USE THE TOOL → MAKE THE GRAPHIC → POST ON LINKEDIN → WRITE THE SUBSTACK
The return arrow closes the loop back to the first step — this repeats per tool
On 'fixed the foundation', a terracotta break mark appears across the FIRST step — the loop can't start if the tools don't work. The ONE accent
Break mark holds ≥2s

beats.narration_text: Here's the method. I don't review a tool from the outside — I use it. If it fits something I'm actually doing, I use it on that. And when a tool has nothing to do with my life, I invent a brand, give it a real problem, and run the tool on that instead. Same rigour either way.

show.event: A vertical rule draws down the centre; two column headings type in
Left column fills in ink as each is named — the tool fits real work
Right column fills in terracotta — the invented brand path
Footer lands: 'never a review from the outside'. Held ≥2s

data.title: I use it, or I invent someone who would

left.heading: When it fits my work
items: Use it on the real task
Say where it got in the way

data.note: never a review from the outside — the write-up is a receipt, not an opinion

beats.narration_text: So before any of the writing, I asked Claude to help me go through every tool on the page, one at a time, honestly.

show.event: Composer framed; spark line reads 'The audit.'
The audit prompt types itself in — the ACTUAL prompt behind the next beat
Terracotta send arms; runningText 'auditing…' — cut to RESULT

props.command: Go through every tool on this page one at a time. For each: does it load, does it run without throwing an error, and does it return something a real user could actually use? Don't grade generously — I have to write about these publicly.

beats.narration_text: The page had been down a long time, so the audit came first. Every tool on the page, one at a time, against three questions. Does it load? Does it run without throwing an error? Does it give you something you could actually use? Anything that failed got fixed before I wrote a word about it.

show.event: Three checks draw in one at a time, each landing ON its spoken question, terracotta marker at the left
Each check's one-line consequence types in beneath it
The closing rule lands and holds: 'fix it before you write about it'. Held ≥2s

data.slideMeta: The audit · every tool, one at a time
data.title: Three questions per tool

items.label: Does it load?
items.why: A dead page is the first thing a new user meets.

items.label: Does it run without erroring?
items.why: Loading is not the same as working.

items.label: Does it return something usable?
items.why: Running is not the same as useful.

data.closer: Anything that failed got fixed before it got written about.

beats.narration_text: Then I built a calendar. Not a content calendar for the algorithm — a tool calendar for me. Every tool gets its own week, so nothing sits unwritten and I never open a blank page wondering which one to cover. The schedule does the deciding.

show.event: A horizontal strip of week slots draws in left to right
The first slot fills with a named tool in terracotta; the rest fill with waiting markers
The strip continues past the frame edge — the schedule keeps going
Footer lands: 'the schedule does the deciding'. Held ≥2s

data.slideMeta: The tool calendar · one tool, one week
data.title: The schedule does the deciding
data.note: one tool a week — so nothing sits unwritten, and no week starts on a blank page

beats.narration_text: And the first article is written. It's on a tool called Ogilvy. It is finished, and it is not posted yet — which is the honest status, not a soft launch. Written, sitting in drafts, going out next.

show.event: A document card draws in, titled with the tool name
Status row lights: WRITTEN in ink
Second status row lights: NOT POSTED in terracotta — the ONE accent, and the honest part
Footer line lands: 'drafts are not launches'. Held ≥2s

data.title: Ogilvy
data.note: drafts are not launches — it goes out next

beats.narration_text: So, the week. One — the tools page works again, every tool audited one at a time. Two — there's a calendar now, so every tool gets a week instead of waiting for inspiration. Three — the first article is written and still unposted. Unglamorous, and it's the part that makes all the rest possible.

show.event: Claude artifact page opens on the cream ground
Four lines stagger in, one per spoken clause
The closing line holds

props.artifactTitle: Every Tool, Every Week. — the week
artifactLines: The tools page works again — every tool audited one at a time, and what failed got fixed.
There's a tool calendar now: every tool gets its own week, so nothing waits for inspiration.
The first article is written — on a tool called Ogilvy — and it is not posted yet.
None of it is glamorous. It is the part that makes the writing worth reading.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. If you maintain something other people are meant to use, paste this: audit my project the way I'd audit it before writing about it publicly — what's actually broken, what's merely embarrassing, and what I'd have to admit if I published today. Then check whether it names the thing you already knew and were avoiding.

The prompt types itself in as the narration reads it aloud, verbatim
Terracotta send arms; runningText 'paste this into Claude…'
Three-item rubric stacks in beneath the composer as each check is spoken

beats.narration_text: Every tool, every week. That's the plan — and now there's a calendar that makes me keep it. I'm Yatra, thanks for watching.
